event_name: Movies at the Strand: Mary Poppins (1964)
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb:
Mary Poppins on the big screen, with a live organ concert to kick things off. Thats not a bad way to spend a Friday night.

The Strand is bringing back the 1964 Disney classic, Julie Andrews, Dick Van Dyke, Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious and all, with a live pre-show performance on the Mighty Allen Theatre Organ 30 minutes before the film starts. If you've got kids who've never seen it on a real screen, this is the version to take them to. If you haven't seen it since you were a kid yourself, same answer.

Check the Strand's site for ticket info and arrive early enough to catch the organ performance. It sets the whole mood.
scoring_notes: Family-friendly option that works for the young families segment of the Perimeter audience. The organ pre-show adds a layer of uniqueness beyond a standard classic film screening. Lower uniqueness score because the Strand does recurring classic film events, but the specific film and organ pairing makes it feel special. Nostalgia appeal also works for empty nesters.

event_name: All Shook Up: The Elvis Presley Musical
blurb:
If you've been looking for a fun Friday night that doesn't involve another crowded restaurant, the Marietta Theatre Company has you covered.

All Shook Up is a full-on Elvis musical built around the classics: Heartbreak Hotel, Hound Dog, Jailhouse Rock, Don't Be Cruel. The plot loosely follows Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, which sounds like a strange combo until you're watching it and realizing it works completely. It's rated PG, it's high energy, and it's the kind of show that's just genuinely fun to be at, the crowd gets into it, the songs are impossible not to sing along to, and you leave in a better mood than you arrived.

Check the Marietta Theatre Company site for exact showtimes and tickets. Worth grabbing dinner nearby beforehand and making a full evening of it.
scoring_notes: Elvis catalog has broad generational appeal that works across 35-65. The Shakespeare-meets-Elvis concept is genuinely interesting. Rated PG makes it accessible across family and adult audiences. Marietta is on the western edge of Perimeter reach but still draws from this audience. Recurring run slightly lowers uniqueness but it's a legitimate theatrical production.

blurb:
Jack Harlow is coming to the Roxy on September 4th, and if you've been on the fence about going, this is worth a hard look.

Harlow puts on a high-energy show and the Roxy is one of the better mid-size venues in Atlanta to actually see a concert, close enough that it feels real, big enough that the production is there. The Battery setup means you can make a full night of it: dinner, the show, drinks after without driving all over town.

Tickets will move, so grab them now rather than watching prices climb closer to the date.
scoring_notes: Jack Harlow skews younger (mid-20s to late-30s), which fits the young professional segment of the Perimeter audience. The Roxy is a proven venue and the Battery location makes logistics easy. Slightly lower audience match since the 38 median age means this won't land for the empty nester segment, but strong for young professionals and couples.

event_name: Concert Featuring the Electromatics at the JCC
blurb:
An outdoor courtyard. Electric blues. A Tuesday evening that actually feels worth leaving the house for.

The Electromatics are playing the Halpern Plaza Courtyard at the MJCCA in Dunwoody, and the description sells itself: sizzling electric blues, soulful vocals, Southern grooves. This is the kind of live music that hits differently outside on a summer night than it does in a club. Two hours, local venue, no complicated logistics.

If you've got a neighbor or a coworker who's always up for a midweek excuse to decompress, this is a solid pick. Check the MJCCA site for ticket info and get there early enough to grab a good spot in the courtyard.
scoring_notes: Dunwoody location is dead center in the Perimeter coverage area. Blues and live outdoor music skew toward 35-55 crowd, which fits the audience. It's a weeknight which limits appeal slightly, but the courtyard setting and approachable format make it a good neighborhood-feel pick.

venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb:
Mamma Mia on the big screen with a margarita bar and a live organ pre-show. If that sentence doesn't already have you texting your friends, I'm not sure what will.

The Strand is doing a full theatrical screening of the Mamma Mia movie, ABBA soundtrack and all, with a margarita bar set up for the occasion and a live concert on the Mighty Allen Theatre Organ starting 30 minutes before the film. It's PG-13, it runs under two hours, and the energy in that room is going to be exactly what you'd hope for. Boas are apparently encouraged.

This is a great girls' night or date night that doesn't require a reservation at a restaurant or a plan that falls apart. Just show up, grab a drink, and let ABBA do the rest.
scoring_notes: Strong adult skew with the margarita + live music + movie format. Mamma Mia has wide nostalgic appeal across women 30-60. The combination of the organ pre-show, margarita bar, and theatrical screening makes this specific night feel distinct from a standard movie outing. Marietta is on the edge of the Perimeter area but still accessible.

event_name: Atlanta Braves vs. Los Angeles Dodgers
blurb:
The Dodgers are coming to Truist Park, and this is not a throwaway series.

Los Angeles versus Atlanta is one of the better rivalries in baseball right now, and getting to watch it in person at Truist Park is the kind of night that actually delivers. First pitch is 7:15 on Thursday, which means you're home by 10:30 if things go well. Grab tickets, get there for batting practice, and grab dinner at the Battery while you're at it.

Tickets are available at a range of price points, so there's no reason to wait on this. A Braves-Dodgers game sells itself.
scoring_notes: Braves baseball is a strong cultural fit for Atlanta-area audiences across all demographics. The Dodgers are a marquee opponent which elevates uniqueness above a typical home game. Household income at $105K makes ticket prices a non-issue. Appeals across the young professional, young family, and empty nester segments.

event_name: Movies & Mimosas: When Harry Met Sally
blurb:
If you've ever quoted this movie at brunch and meant it, Saturday morning is calling your name.

Springs Cinema is running their Movies & Mimosas series this weekend, and the pick is When Harry Met Sally. Classic Nora Ephron, Billy Crystal, Meg Ryan, the fake deli scene. Every ticket includes a mimosa, and you're watching it in heated recliners at the taphouse, which is already a better Saturday morning than most people are planning.

This is a great one to grab a friend for. It's local, it's relaxed, it's under two hours, and you'll be done before noon with plenty of weekend left. Don't overthink it.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for the adult-leaning Perimeter audience, especially women 30-55. When Harry Met Sally is a crowd-pleaser with wide recognition across the age range. The Movies & Mimosas format is a recurring series, which lowers uniqueness slightly, but this specific film screening on this date is its own event. Sandy Springs location is right in the coverage area.

event_name: Two Fires One Pot: Vineyard to Island Table Pop-Up Dining Experience
blurb:
Six courses. Caribbean-inspired. Right here in Dunwoody.

Two Fires One Pot is teaming up with Vino Venue for a pop-up tasting dinner called Vineyard to Island Table, and the concept alone is worth showing up for. We're talking a full six-course, Caribbean-inspired menu in a setting that pairs island flavors with serious wine curation. It's not a restaurant night. It's a produced dining experience, the kind where every course is intentional and the whole evening has an arc.

Pop-up dinners like this don't stick around. The date is Sunday, the experience is specific, and once it sells out, it's gone. If you've been looking for a reason to actually do something interesting this weekend instead of defaulting to your usual dinner spot, this is it. Grab your person and get a reservation.
scoring_notes: Pop-up elevated dining is a strong fit for a $105K median income, adult-skewing audience in Dunwoody. Six-course tasting menus appeal to the young professional and empty nester segments. High uniqueness since it's a one-night pop-up with a specific culinary concept, not a recurring weekly thing.

blurb:
Jack Harlow at the Roxy on a Friday night is a solid pick if you've got college-age kids home for the summer or just want a high-energy concert right at the Battery. He's had a run of genuinely good music over the last few years, the kind of artist where even if you're not his core audience, you know the songs.

The Coca-Cola Roxy is one of the better mid-size venues in Atlanta. Not too big to feel impersonal, not so small that you're crammed in. And being at the Battery means dinner before or drinks after are built right in.

Tickets will move for this one. September 4th, 7:30pm. If this is on anyone's radar, sooner is better.
scoring_notes: Jack Harlow skews younger than East Cobb's median age of 42, but the audience has college-age kids and the Battery proximity keeps it relevant. Not the strongest demographic fit for the core readership, but included because the Battery connection and the Roxy's quality make it a credible pick for the younger end of the audience or parents looking for something to do with their kids who are home for the summer.

event_name: Sundays in the Park: "The American Heritage, in Brass"
blurb:
Free live music in Roswell's Town Square on a Sunday evening is a pretty hard thing to argue with. The Roswell New Horizons Pops Band is a 40-member ensemble, and this week they're joined by the Dogwood Brass Quintet and special guests from the Atlanta Accordion Club for a program called The American Heritage, in Brass.

It's an outdoor concert, which means you show up, find a spot, and let the evening come to you. The music is patriotic and classic American, the kind of stuff that sounds exactly right in an open park as summer winds down.

Doors open at 5:30pm. It's free. It's Roswell. That's a pretty easy Sunday.
scoring_notes: Free outdoor concerts in Roswell Town Square are part of a recurring series, which keeps uniqueness lower. But the specific program (brass quintet plus accordion club as special guests) is a one-time lineup, which gives it some distinction. Broad appeal for the older end of the East Cobb demographic. Easy, low-commitment format works well as a supporting pick even if it's not the top featured event.

event_name: Talking Tech: Reliving Apollo 11 with John Baumbusch
venue: Roswell Cultural Arts Center area (see event page), Roswell
blurb:
If you were alive in 1969, you remember where you were. If you weren't, you've probably still sat through enough documentaries to feel the weight of what Apollo 11 actually pulled off. Either way, this Saturday afternoon presentation at Roswell is worth an hour of your time.

John Baumbusch is walking through the full story of humanity's first Moon landing, the technology, the people, the stakes, and everything that had to go exactly right for it to work. It's a Talking Tech event, so this isn't a dry lecture, it's built to be engaging and accessible.

It's a 1pm Saturday. You'll be home in time for whatever else you had planned. For the curious and the space-obsessed alike, this is a GREAT way to spend a lunch hour.
scoring_notes: East Cobb's highly educated, 42-median-age audience skews toward intellectual programming. Apollo 11 has massive nostalgia pull for the older half of the audience and genuine fascination for the younger half. Saturday afternoon timing is low-barrier. The Talking Tech series format suggests a quality production. Docked slightly on uniqueness because it's a recurring series, but the Apollo 11 subject matter is specific enough to treat it as a one-off.

venue: Jim R. Miller Parks & Event Center, Marietta
blurb:
The Cobb International Festival is back at Jim R. Miller Park this Saturday, and it's exactly what it sounds like: food, music, cultural performances, arts vendors, and a kids' corner, all celebrating the diverse communities that make up Cobb County. It's a genuine community event, not a tourist trap dressed up as one.

For families with teens, this is a solid Saturday activity that doesn't require a ton of planning. Show up, eat interesting food, catch a performance or two, browse the vendors. The format is relaxed enough that you can stay two hours or five, depending on how the day unfolds.

It's local, it's free to attend, and it's one of the better reasons to actually use a Saturday afternoon instead of watching it disappear.
scoring_notes: Annual community festival with broad family appeal. East Cobb's mix of established families and empty nesters both fit here. The educational, culturally curious slant matches the 65% college-educated audience well. Not the most unique event on the list since it's a recurring annual event, but it's a once-a-year thing in Cobb County's backyard, which still gives it legs.

event_name: When Rivers Meet: The Black and Jewish Origins of America's Sound
blurb:
What do the blues and Broadway have in common? More than you'd think. When Rivers Meet traces the shared musical DNA of the Black and Jewish American experience, specifically how those two traditions collided and created the soundtrack of 20th century America. Jazz, blues, Broadway, rock and roll, it all flows from those two rivers meeting.

This is a live performance led by a celebrated vocalist, not a lecture, not a panel. It's music, story, and history woven together into something that actually sticks with you when you leave.

It's a Sunday at 4pm in Roswell, which makes for a genuinely easy afternoon. The kind of cultural outing that makes you feel like you actually did something with your weekend, because you did.
scoring_notes: East Cobb's highly educated, higher-income audience responds well to arts programming with intellectual substance. This event is genuinely uncommon, a music-driven exploration of American cultural history, not a standard concert or play. The Sunday 4pm timing is easy and low-commitment. Slightly lower audience_match because it skews more toward the empty nester end of the demographic than families with teens.

event_name: All Shook Up: The Elvis Presley Musical
blurb:
If you grew up with Elvis on the radio or just have a soft spot for a good jukebox musical, this one is right in your wheelhouse. All Shook Up is a full-on theatrical production built around Elvis Presley's greatest hits, with a plot that's basically Shakespeare's Twelfth Night dropped into 1955 small-town America. It sounds like it shouldn't work. It absolutely does.

Theatre in the Square is a Marietta institution, and this is the final weekend of the run. August 21st and 22nd are your last chances to catch it, Friday and Saturday both at 8pm. After that, it's gone.

This is a great pick if you've been meaning to get out to the theatre more. Low commitment, familiar music, and genuinely fun storytelling. Grab a couple of tickets and make an evening of it in downtown Marietta.
scoring_notes: East Cobb's median age of 42, high education level, and strong homeownership rate all point to an audience that appreciates live arts. Elvis is cross-generational and broadly appealing. The final weekend urgency is real, not manufactured. Theatre in the Square is a known local venue, which reduces friction. Good fit for couples and empty nesters especially.

blurb:
Picture this: a Saturday afternoon at the Battery, a handcrafted margarita made with Hornitos Tequila in one hand, a taco from a local food truck in the other, and a live mariachi band doing their thing about 20 feet away. That's the whole vibe at the Marg & Taco Fest coming to Live! at the Battery this Saturday, August 22nd.

This isn't a farmers market with a food tent slapped on the side. It's a full fiesta takeover, taco trucks, craft margaritas, local vendors, and live music all rolled into one afternoon out. It's the kind of thing you drag a few friends to and end up staying way longer than you planned.

The Battery is right in your backyard. Use it.
scoring_notes: East Cobb households at $118K median income have no issue spending on a fun Saturday out. The Battery is extremely close and familiar to this audience. This is a one-day special event, not a weekly fixture, which gives it real can't-miss energy. The adult social skew works well for this mix of established families and empty nesters who want a fun night out without it being a formal commitment.

event_name: Atlanta Braves vs. Los Angeles Dodgers
blurb:
Look, there are Braves games and then there are Braves vs. Dodgers games. This is the latter. The Dodgers are one of the biggest franchises in baseball right now, which means the energy at Truist Park on Wednesday night is going to be a few notches above your average Tuesday in July.

Truist Park is basically East Cobb's front yard. You probably drive past it on your way somewhere at least once a week. But there's something about a marquee matchup that actually gets you in the seats instead of just watching from the couch.

First pitch is at 7:15pm on August 26th. Grab a few tickets, head over to the Battery for dinner first, and make a proper night of it.
scoring_notes: Truist Park is literally in East Cobb's backyard, which gives this a hyper-local relevance that no other event on the list can match. The Dodgers are a premium opponent, which elevates a standard game into a marquee matchup. $118K median income means tickets are a non-issue. Strong cross-generational appeal for families and empty nesters alike. Slight hit on uniqueness because it's a single MLB game in a long season, not a truly rare one-night event.

venue: Jim R. Miller Park & Event Center, Marietta
blurb:
Global food, live music, and performances from cultures all across Cobb County, and it doesn't cost you a thing to walk in.

The Cobb County International Festival lands at Jim R. Miller Park on Saturday from 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM. It's a celebration of the diversity that's been quietly building in this county for years, brought out into the open with food vendors, visual arts, and performing artists representing heritages from around the world. Five hours of it, right in your backyard.

Bring the family or go solo. It's the kind of afternoon that's easy to show up to with no agenda, wander around for a couple of hours, eat something you've never tried before, and leave in a genuinely good mood. No tickets, no hassle, just show up.
scoring_notes: Free, family-friendly, and community-rooted. Fits East Cobb's mix of established families and empty nesters who are civically engaged. Saturday timing is ideal. Less unique than a one-night competition, but the cultural angle and zero cost make it broadly accessible and worth including.
